rapport_notes: Professional and courteous but somewhat mechanical; minimal warmth or personality; customer felt transactional, not heard.
process_discipline_notes: Damage coverage (Sheet 1) mentioned in Stage 2 takeaway but no evidence it was raised as a customer concern in Stage 1, making the placement technically correct but not validated by prior discovery.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: MISSING — rep launched directly into address confirmation: 'Let me just confirm our pickup location is at 3550 Robinson road...'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive logistics probing: 'Alright. Before I discuss the pricing structure and your estimate, do you have any concern about the moving process.' Customer answered 'No.' — came too late, after 15+ minutes of location/furniture questions.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised zero concerns; agenda question drew 'No,' leaving nothing to probe deeper on.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Covered in Stage 2 as part of takeaway: 'First is we do have the no worry damage coverage which provides up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for any accidental damages.'
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: MISSING — never mentioned Meet Your Mover, named crew lead, or who specifically will show up.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Covered in Stage 2: 'Also we have the on time guarantee if we cannot make it at the time we do that we arrange we immediately start discounting money of the final bill.'
evidence_quotes.communication: MISSING — no mention of day-before call, named crew lead follow-up, or inbox updates.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full: 'So for this move I estimate them to finish in, in seven hours to eight hours with two movers and one truck. So the estimated cost for that is a $1,578 to $1,782.' + personalization: 'However, the drive time could be between one hour to one and a half depending on the traffic moving into a two story house. So for this move I estimate...'
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_window: 'But then, of course this is only my estimate. So, if ever that the move takes less than this, then you will only be charged for how much time we use during the move.'
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: 'So, let's say for example, you are really ready on the move day like the movers will just focus unloading everything into the truck then that would really help keep the time down. So, obviously the last time you take, the less money you end up spending at the end of the day.'
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip: Implied in the above — customer prep reduces time/cost, but not framed as an explicit 'anything you get done before we show up comes off your bill' statement.
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair: MISSING — no 'Does that feel fair?' and no silence-hold after any open-ended question.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock: MISSING — never stated 'your rate locks when you book.'
evidence_quotes.explicit_close_ask: No explicit ask such as 'Would you like our help with your move?' Instead: 'Would you like to schedule your move now for October 14th?' When customer declined, rep pivoted to email without re-engaging on the rate-lock or an alternative close.

top_strength: Excellent logistics probing and estimate anchor — rep gathered precise apartment/destination details (floor, elevator access, parking, furniture specifics, distances) and delivered a well-reasoned 7–8 hour range with clear drive-time and move-type reasoning, showing competence in scoping.
coaching_note: Open with quid pro quo framing (time-boxed promise + accurate quote exchange) immediately, ask their agenda before any logistics questions, and when they have zero concerns, do not skip the full Sheet 1–4 takeaway; deliver all four differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, on-time, communication) at the end so nothing is left on the table.
